[h1] NEON, NEON, ONE screwing NEON [/h1]

Neon Drive is an arcade game that markets itself as a rhythm game, but unfortunately, it kind of just leeches off the 80s Miami aesthetic. And, frankly, it doesn't even pull it off at an amateur level.  

The game offers an 8-level mode split into 3 difficulty levels (with two checkpoints at around 35% and 70% progress, and the only differences being speed modifiers – on higher difficulties, there aren’t any new obstacles), plus an endurance mode, which is basically a compilation of the same levels, probably meant to see how long a player can handle the repetitive music and gameplay before getting nauseous. You control one of 8 cars, which, unfortunately, you can’t pick to your liking, though you can change up to 4 letters on the license plate. It’s weird, but that’s how it is.

Among the few positives, you can mention the level design and themes. Sure, the Steam description overhypes it, saying "Neon Drive has it all: from beautiful city jungle and ocean road landscapes to exploding enemy spaceships," but the neon line effects and synthwave vibes come across pretty well. You can also note that button presses match the music rhythm, though this is subjective since not all presses hit the beat. 

However, the drawbacks far outweigh the few good points. Hitbox issues, caused by awkward camera angles, mean it’s sometimes hard to tell exactly when to switch lanes, leading to unavoidable crashes. The microtiming demands from these hitbox problems require super quick reactions and rapid button presses, which quickly tires out your fingers.

The controls feel unresponsive and non-adaptive: the car reacts to inputs with a noticeable delay, even with smoothing turned off and graphics set to minimum. As for adaptive controls: for example, when the car turns into a transformer, a spaceship, or flies from the sky to the ground while dodging oncoming traffic, jumps and slides aren’t controlled by the “up” and “down” buttons, but by “left” and “right.”

And finally, the special effects look unfinished. The graphics might be okay for an amateur level, but the blurring and lane changes look jerky and rough.

Neon Drive is not recommended. The game isn’t worth your time, even if you just want to collect cards or achievements, which would be hard to earn because of the clunky controls.

Neon Drive, developed by Fraoula and Spiky Crumb and published by Fraoula, is a rhythm-driven arcade game that masterfully fuses high-speed action with retro aesthetics. Set in a neon-drenched cyberpunk world, the game immediately immerses players in a visually striking environment where vibrant colors, pulsing lights, and dynamic backgrounds create a strong sense of motion and urgency. Its visual style draws inspiration from 1980s arcade games and synthwave culture, giving the game a distinctive, nostalgic charm while maintaining a modern polish that keeps the experience engaging. The combination of futuristic visuals and energetic design makes every level feel like a journey through a digital neon landscape, with each segment presenting new visual motifs and challenges that keep players captivated.

At its core, Neon Drive revolves around reflex-based gameplay where the player controls a vehicle speeding forward along multiple lanes. The simplicity of lane-switching mechanics belies the depth of skill required to navigate increasingly complex obstacles. Players must time their movements with precision, often reacting in split seconds to avoid collisions. As the game progresses, new mechanics such as flying sequences and side-scrolling action sequences are introduced, keeping the gameplay fresh and testing the player's adaptability. Despite the escalating difficulty, the game provides checkpoints and practice modes, allowing players to gradually improve and approach each challenge with a sense of mastery. This balance between intense difficulty and thoughtful support systems creates a satisfying learning curve that encourages repeated playthroughs.

One of the game’s most notable strengths is its soundtrack, which features original synthwave compositions crafted to complement the high-paced gameplay. Each track is tightly integrated with the action, creating a rhythm-driven experience where players often find themselves moving in sync with the beat. The music not only enhances immersion but also subtly guides the player, providing auditory cues that anticipate upcoming obstacles and inform timing decisions. This synergy between music and gameplay makes Neon Drive feel like a cohesive, living rhythm game rather than just a series of mechanical challenges.

The level design further reinforces the game’s appeal. Neon Drive offers eight main stages, each with unique visual and gameplay elements that prevent monotony and maintain a sense of progression. Environments shift from linear cityscapes to more abstract neon arenas, introducing new patterns of obstacles that challenge players’ timing and reflexes. The combination of varying stage layouts, visual flair, and increasingly intricate patterns ensures that players remain engaged and motivated to push through even the toughest sections.

Overall, Neon Drive stands out as a polished and challenging rhythm-arcade experience. Its vibrant neon aesthetic, compelling soundtrack, and well-designed gameplay mechanics work together to create a game that is both visually stunning and mechanically rewarding. While its difficulty may be daunting for some, the inclusion of practice options and gradual difficulty scaling makes the challenge feel fair rather than punishing. For players who enjoy rhythm games, reflex tests, or simply a visually immersive arcade adventure, Neon Drive offers a thoroughly satisfying and memorable experience.

Rating: 8/10

Neon Drive — настоящая находка для всех любителей аркадных гонок! Эта стильная и энергичная игра мгновенно привлекает внимание своей яркой неоновой графикой и драйвовым саундтреком, создающими уникальное настроение футуристического мира.

Простота управления и интуитивно понятный интерфейс позволяют быстро освоиться даже новичкам, однако игра обладает достаточным уровнем сложности, чтобы заинтересовать опытных геймеров. Каждая трасса представляет собой настоящее испытание на реакцию и внимательность, заставляющее вновь и вновь возвращаться за новыми рекордами.

Особое восхищение вызывает звуковое сопровождение — каждая мелодия идеально сочетается с ритмом гонки, наполняя экран энергией и адреналином. А стильный дизайн автомобилей и окружающей среды лишь усиливает впечатления от каждой минуты, проведенной в игре.

Neon Drive идеально подходит для короткого перерыва или долгой сессии вечером, предлагая море удовольствия и позитива. Если вам нравятся яркие цвета, высокая скорость и азарт погони, то эта игра непременно должна оказаться в вашей коллекции!

i really really wanted to like this game like so bad and i do but i also dont. i wanted to play a game like this because i like that 80s/90s theme. the music in the game is good and the game controllers are just ok not too bad but there are some levels that just make you want to quit a lot. i get that this is supposed to be a arcade style game but its not great feeling very janky. the space part were you shoot the asteroids is cool and i liked it a lot it reminds me of older games but it is also hard to know were the end of the screen is because i cant tell sometimes if im fully over to the other side of the screen. the jet part that is over the water is also cool but it makes me a bit dizzy and the controllers are too janky to make it fun. the style and graphics of the game is good tho i really like the way the game looks. the transformer part is not fun and did not like it very much but i can see it being good with a bit more polish. i also think some of the road blocks are way too close to gether sometimes making it much harder than it should to dodge them it feels janky sometimes it is fun and has a nice rhythm but other times feels too stressful for a game like this. the game is also way too short not a lot of levels. i really looked foreword to trying this game to. at least it was fun for the first 5 minutes of the game ill give this game a 4.5 out of 10 and also i wish there was a no fail option to the game so you can just have fun with out loosing and make the music sound like its skipping.
